articles.title: Horror as another suspect polling firm vanishes amid scrutiny: 'Major scandal'
articles.description: The election forecasting community was rattled this week by reporting that Wedgewood Polls, a recent upstart firm, had been fabricating most or all of its data. Now another polling firm is in experts' crosshairs — but they seem to have deleted their entire internet presence before anything could be proven. FiftyPlusOne, a polling analysis site, announced in a blog post on Thursday it is ending its use of SoCal Strategies’ surveys after the pollster’s web presence disappeared a few days after FiftyPlusOne asked to check its data. FiftyPlusOne interviewed a person calling himself Wilson Rochford, the firm’s head pollster, on October 20. He promised to send raw data by Friday to substantiate disputed surveys, and said Jack Sims, who had been tied to Wedgewood, “didn’t actually have a big role” in polling. FiftyPlusOne says it hasn’t heard back since, and that the Washington Post reported the firm’s website and X account were gone. The site says it can’t confirm basic facts about the business or its people. A Florida company Sims set up was dissolved in May, with no replacement found. VoteHub’s Zachary Donnini said the head pollster at Wedgewood told him he attended Boston University and had worked with SoCal Strategies, details that fit Rochford. FiftyPlusOne is removing two SoCal Strategies polls in particular, which it says are missing crosstab data and don't look like any of the rest of the firm's output. The new report triggered shockwaves among social media observers. "This polling situation is a hair's breadth away from becoming a major, major scandal," wrote Fox News Digital columnist David Marcus. "Seems pretty clear at this point that the polling industry needs to be regulated," wrote political columnist Alex Zeldin. "Seems like @50plus1news is becoming the Isaac Chotiner of polling investigations," wrote Blueprint Polls lead pollster Evan Roth Smith.

articles.title: Judge orders Trump deposition in defamation suit against the BBC by Dec. 11
articles.description: A federal judge has ordered President Donald Trump to sit for a deposition in his defamation lawsuit against the BBC by Dec. 11. The order Thursday from U.S. Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett came as the BBC’s lawyers complained that Trump had delayed his appearance. Attorney Charles Tobin said that with two months left in the discovery period, “we still haven’t been able to depose the plaintiff.” Lett said Trump must sit for a deposition by Dec. 11 or face sanctions up to dismissal of his lawsuit unless the discovery period was extended past Dec. 18. Trump is bringing the case over a BBC documentary called “Trump: A Second Chance.”

articles.title: Serb voters abroad face long trips in tight election
articles.description: Serbian voters overseas are facing major hurdles in casting their ballots in a tight parliamentary election this weekend. The vote is a showdown between the populist strongman Aleksandar Vucic and a student movement behind nearly two years of protests. Critics say Vucic's government is doing all it can to discourage some 100,000 people who have registered to vote abroad and many of whom may support the students. Authorities have denied this. But some polling stations in the U.S., for example, will be open partly overnight to match the Serbian time zone.

articles.title: Opinion: Trump May Not Be a Russian ‘Asset,’ But He’s Definitely Putin’s Stooge
articles.description: Is our president a Russian asset? He sure acts like one as he waives Lindsey Graham’s sanctions on Russia while greenlighting a diesel deal that delivers billions of American dollars to the Kremlin’s war machine. Maybe Putin has “kompromat” on Trump. Or maybe not. Perhaps all he needs to have is the level of power Trump can’t seem to wield here in the U.S., despite his best (worst) efforts. It’s also possible all this to Russia with love posturing is just Trump acting out of frustration. He and his party are on a path to suffer a midterm debacle, and he’s trying to change the equation by shifting the blame and the focus from his ill-chosen war with Iran. Read more at The Daily Beast.
